1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	OXIDE v2 (branch `rewrite/v2`): a structural context engine for agents. One Python package, `oxide`, in `src/oxide/` (ADR-0011); the Rust/Bun implementation it replaced is recoverable at `f79808a`.
4	`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file, so Claude and Codex share one root policy.
5	
6	The architecture authority is `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, with standing rules and research verdicts in `docs/decisions.md`, the evaluation protocol in `fixtures/eval/README.md` and decisions in `docs/adr/` (Proposed ADRs are proposals, not Accepted decisions; never change an ADR's status unasked). When they disagree with anything else in the repo, they win.
7	
8	This file is always loaded; keep it short. New commands go in `docs/agents/workflow.md`; the public API is documented in `docs/public-api.md`.
9	
10	## Layout and ownership
11	
12	- `src/oxide/api.py`, `models.py`: the public API and its typed results/errors, the stable product boundary.
13	- `src/oxide/core/`: repository intelligence and deterministic policy (Python slice, derivation, retrieval, TreeRouter, selection/packing). No filesystem or database access except through the read view it is given.
14	- `src/oxide/capture.py`, `src/oxide/storage/`: worktree capture; LadybugDB ownership, generations, publication and queries. Nothing else touches LadybugDB.
15	- `src/oxide/cli.py`, `src/oxide/mcp_server.py` (FastMCP) and future editor adapters: Python clients of `oxide.api` only. They must not parse source, route, select or pack.
16	- Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Judges, if ever added, are optional external services.
17	- Toolchain: Mise is the entrypoint (`mise run verify`, which CI runs); uv manages Python and dependencies (`pyproject.toml`, committed `uv.lock`); pytest, Ruff, mypy `--strict`. Rust, Bun/TypeScript, pnpm, Deno and `packages/*` are retired; don't reintroduce them without an ADR.
18	
19	## How to work
20	
21	- For fully-autonomous tasks, don't poll background tasks; they will send you their output once they're done.
22	- Keep it simple. Build only what the current phase needs: no speculative abstractions, flags or features.
23	- Don't duplicate logic, policy or docs. Still, don't add an abstraction just to remove a few repeated lines.
24	- Keep changes small and cohesive. Don't clean up unrelated code during a focused task.
25	- Reuse existing patterns and dependencies before adding new ones. A new package or dependency needs a reuse, packaging or API reason (SPEC § System architecture).
26	- Keep the public API and versioned formats (derivation components, store schema, payload/units versions) compatible unless the task says to change them; bump the version when you do. Legacy v1 compatibility (SQLite indexes, symbol ids, CLI/MCP/JSON surface) and the retired Rust/TS protocol are not requirements (SPEC § Compatibility policy).
27	- Fix root causes. Don't weaken tests, regenerate goldens or re-baseline just to make a failure go away.
28	- Implementation first: the default loop is read the code, change it, add or adjust a test, `mise run verify`; before a push also `mise run pythons` (CI's 3.12/3.14 rows). Feature, bug-fix, language and refactor work needs no study, preregistration or report.
29	- An experiment is only for claims a test can't settle: a retrieval/routing/packing quality change (ContextBench gates, `docs/agents/workflow.md`), a performance claim (measure before and after with `scripts/bench.py`), or promoting an optional judge. Then fix the pass/fail rule before reading held-out results, and record the verdict (one row in `docs/decisions.md` § Research verdicts, plus a short report only if a gate, test or comment will cite it).
30	- Read the code, tests and docs before stating how something works. Label each claim as measured or inferred.
31	- If missing or ambiguous information could change the implementation, check the repo first. If that doesn't settle it, ask one focused question instead of guessing. Don't invent permanent ID/schema/transport/model policy to unblock scaffolding (`docs/decisions.md` rule 4).
32	- Before finishing, read the full diff for accidental changes in scope, public API surface (`oxide/__init__.py`), dependencies (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`) or generated files.
33	- Tests never touch real user data: every test and subprocess gets a private data location (`tests/python/conftest.py`).
34	- Don't commit, push, tag, release, edit GitHub issues or roadmaps, or start the next phase unless approved.
35	- Keep every OXIDE source file at or below 500 LOC. Tests, docs and CSS are exempt, and so are vendored or generated agent tooling (`.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode/`), which stay as their tools ship them. Markdown is documentation, not source. Split a source file before completion if your change takes it over the limit.
36	- If unsure about a problem or a bug, search relevant sources of the problem before tackling it.
37	
38	## Read before touching
39	
40	| Area | Read first |
41	|---|---|
42	| Anything architectural | `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/adr/` |
43	| Python engine, storage, removed/retained features | `docs/adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md`, `docs/public-api.md` |
44	| Build, test, lint, commit format | `docs/agents/workflow.md` |
45	| Issues, triage labels, domain docs | `docs/agents/` (`issue-tracker.md`, `triage-labels.md`, `domain.md`) |
46	| Historical evidence and legacy reproduction | `docs/decisions.md` (verdicts; reports and the migration audit are pinned at `013e791`). Port semantic lessons only where current SPEC requires them; legacy layout and APIs are not v2 instructions. |
47	| v2 review policy | `docs/review/` — reviewer-facing invariants for the Python engine (public API, storage/generations, core/retrieval, capture/language, evidence/benchmarks). Architecture authority remains `docs/spec/SPEC.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. |
48	
49	## Always-on rules
50	
51	- Legacy code and docs are historical evidence, not a template (SPEC, `docs/decisions.md` rule 2). The old implementation is recoverable from `main` / `ac985b28`; don't port it into `src/oxide/` without a stated SPEC requirement.
52	- Retrieval, routing and packing changes are evaluated per SPEC § Evaluation against the frozen baselines (`tests/python/test_baseline.py` checks Phase 3 exactly); never regenerate a frozen artifact to make a failure pass. Legacy numbers in pinned historical reports are historical comparators, not v2 gates.
53	- Models judge; deterministic code decides. Keep JEV and learned judges optional; there are no embeddings. The deterministic offline path needs no model or network (only `oxide prepare` fetches the pinned FTS extension, explicitly).
54	- Let native libraries do recursive and latency-sensitive work (tree-sitter queries, LadybugDB queries, Networkx for graph algorithms); Python holds bounded policy.
55

57	## CodeGraph
58	
59	In repositories indexed by CodeGraph (a `.codegraph/` directory exists at the repo root), reach for it BEFORE grep/find or reading files when you need to understand or locate code:
60	
61	- **MCP tool** (when available): `codegraph_explore` answers most code questions in one call — the relevant symbols' verbatim source plus the call paths between them, including dynamic-dispatch hops grep can't follow. Name a file or symbol in the query to read its current line-numbered source. If it's listed but deferred, load it by name via tool search.
62	- **Shell** (always works): `codegraph explore "<symbol names or question>"` prints the same output.
63	
64	If there is no `.codegraph/` directory, skip CodeGraph entirely — indexing is the user's decision.

content.text:
I've tightened `AGENTS.md`, which `CLAUDE.md` links to, so Claude and Codex both get the change. Nothing else in the repo changed.

The "How to work" section now leads with six concise rules:

- **Implementation first:** read the code, change it, test, run `mise run verify` (plus `mise run pythons` before a push). Feature, bug-fix, language and refactor work gets no study, plan doc or report.
- **Library first:** use an existing helper, the standard library or an installed dependency (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX) before writing your own code. I folded the old "native libraries do the heavy work" rule into this one.
- **No speculative abstractions:** no flags, options or features beyond what the current phase needs.
- **Minimal documentation:** update only the doc that owns the changed fact. No new design notes, plans or reports unless asked or a gate cites them. Comments explain why, not what.
- **Algorithm-driven graph selection:** use a named, standard graph algorithm (NetworkX or a LadybugDB query) with a stated goal, not hand-tuned weights or ad-hoc traversal.
- **Benchmark-backed decisions:** a quality or performance claim needs before/after numbers from the ContextBench gates or `scripts/bench.py`. Set the pass/fail rule before reading held-out results, and record one verdict row in `docs/decisions.md`. No numbers means no claim and no merge.

The old experiment rule is now a single line pointing back to the benchmark rule. The file is 71 lines (7 added, 6 removed).

Two things to check:
- **Possible conflict with ADR-0012:** the graph-selection rule may clash with the Proposed ADR-0012, which says NetworkX is not used for ranking. That ADR isn't Accepted, so I didn't change it, but you may want to reconcile the two.
- **Nothing ran:** I didn't run `mise run verify` (this was a docs-only change), and nothing is committed.
